record.paper_title: Open Questions on Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics of Chemical Reaction Networks
record.original_question: How can nonequilibrium thermodynamics of chemical reaction networks be extended to research directions involving nonisothermal effects, non-ideal solutions, photochemistry, and electrochemistry, and how might progress on those extensions affect the study of chemical complexity in metabolism, chemical information processing, origins of life, and biogeochemistry?

evidence.quote: I have only sketched some of the promising research directions enabled by the recent developments in nonequilibrium thermodynamics of CRN, and many more could have been mentioned (e.g. nonisothermal effects, non-ideal solutions, photo- and electro-chemistry).
I expect that much progress will happen in the years to come which has the potential to impact our understanding of metabolism, chemical information processing, origins of life, and biogeochemistry.

artifact.category_tag: nonequilibrium thermodynamics of chemical reaction networks
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a broad research-program direction rather than a single sharp conjecture. Partial extensions exist (e.g., thermodynamics of non-ideal CRNs by Avanzini–Falasco–Esposito, electrochemical and photochemical CRN thermodynamics formulations), but no unified framework simultaneously covering nonisothermal, non-ideal, photochemical, and electrochemical CRNs with full second-law and fluctuation-theorem structure has been established. The overall program is open.

status_evidence.title: Thermodynamics of non-ideal chemical reaction networks
status_evidence.snippet: Avanzini, Falasco, Esposito extend CRN thermodynamics to non-ideal solutions, addressing one of the listed directions but not the combined program.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress on the non-ideal solutions component.

status_evidence.title: Open Questions on Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics of Chemical Reaction Networks

status_evidence.claim: The combined extensions are flagged as open research directions.
